description: Two-book strategy classification (docs/INVESTMENTS-PAGE-SPEC.md, 'Strategy model & policy deviations'). CORE = $1T+ durables: never sell, delta-10 covered calls, forced exits must be recovered (re-buy or sell puts until re-assigned). INVENTORY = volatile wheel names: sell puts for premium, on assignment exit via delta-20 calls; holding them passively is the deviation. Symbols are Neel's declaration, not an API lookup — edit here when policy changes. Seeded by Claude 2026-07-12 from known market caps; TSLA and IBIT classifications flagged for Neel's review. GOOG added 2026-07-22 alongside GOOGL -- same company (Alphabet Class C vs Class A), was incorrectly falling through to 'unclassified'/Tier-2 wheel treatment. AMD classified Inventory 2026-07-22 (market cap $924B just under $1T, trading history matched wheel behavior) then moved to Core 2026-07-23 on Neel's explicit override -- his call, not a data correction.
